identity.title: CompVLA: A Variable Compliance Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-rich Manipulation
identity.repo_note: The project page and the paper describe a released demonstration dataset. No public training repository was found in this pass.

summary: CompVLA adds a second flow-matching expert to a pi0-style VLA. The action expert predicts a TCP twist and gripper command. The compliance expert, conditioned on that trajectory, predicts a diagonal stiffness and a virtual displacement. A geometric impedance controller turns those into directional compliance and a pressing force. The paper learns stiffness Kd, not a proportional gain Kp. The local landscape row's Kp label is therefore the planning note, not the paper's output. No code was linked because no repository was released in the sources opened here.

landscape.paradigm: Variable-compliance VLA. The local note says Kp and Kd plus actions. The paper's learned compliance outputs are diagonal stiffness and virtual displacement.

model.overview: A pi0 backbone (PaliGemma VLM plus an action expert) gains a compliance expert initialized by copying the action expert. Both experts attend to the VLM with a blockwise causal mask. Weights start from lerobot/pi0_base. The compliance expert also sees a 13-d relative-pose condition packed into the noisy compliance input.

objectives.name: Noisy target path
objectives.explanation: Tau 1 is noise and tau 0 is the data. Because inference integrates from 1 to 0, the regression target is epsilon minus Y.

symbols.meaning: Clean action sequence or clean compliance sequence.
Gaussian noise of the same shape.

objectives.name: Joint flow-matching loss
objectives.explanation: The action expert is conditioned on the observation and language. The compliance expert is also conditioned on the relative TCP trajectory. During training that trajectory is the demonstration. During inference it is the action expert's prediction. Joint angles are an auxiliary training target and are dropped at inference.

symbols.meaning: TCP twists and gripper commands over the chunk.
Diagonal stiffness and virtual displacement over the chunk.
Relative TCP poses and gripper commands, eq. 8.

train.text: Initialize from pi0_base and copy the action expert into the compliance expert.
Build stiffness and virtual-displacement labels from the demonstrated wrench. Learn Kd only.

sources.locator: Section on directional compliance and force modulation

train.text: Sample tau and noise, form the straight path, and regress both vector fields. Condition the compliance expert on the dataset trajectory Z_t.
Train 100k steps at batch 32 in bfloat16 with the AdamW schedule above. Keep joint-angle channels as an auxiliary target.

infer.text: From images, language, and robot state, denoise the action expert for 10 steps to a TCP twist and gripper command.
Integrate the twist into a reference trajectory and condition the compliance expert on it.
Deform the reference pose by the predicted virtual displacement and run geometric impedance control with the predicted diagonal stiffness. Do not read the wrist wrench.

task.action: TCP twist and gripper, plus diagonal stiffness and a 6-d virtual displacement. Chunk length T=25.
task.horizon: Inference denoises the action expert for 10 steps. Logs are synchronized at 10 Hz.
task.contact: Training labels come from the interaction wrench. Inference inputs are images and joints. The low-level law is geometric impedance.
